questions.prompt: A population has mean \(50\) and variance \(144\). For samples of size \(64\), find \(E(\bar X)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)\).
questions.answer: For a sample mean, \(E(\bar X)=\mu=50\). Also \[\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}=\frac{144}{64}=2.25.\]

questions.prompt: A population has standard deviation \(5\). What is the standard error of \(\bar X\) for \(n=100\)?
questions.answer: The standard error is \(\sigma/\sqrt n\). Hence \[\operatorname{se}(\bar X)=\frac{5}{\sqrt{100}}=0.5.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(20\) and standard deviation \(5\). For \(n=100\), estimate \(P(\bar X>21)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(5/\sqrt{100}=0.5\). Thus \(z=(21-20)/0.5=2\), so \[P(\bar X>21)\approx1-\Phi(2)=0.0228.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(10\) and standard deviation \(3\). For \(n=36\), estimate \(P(\bar X<9)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(3/6=0.5\). The z-score is \((9-10)/0.5=-2\), so \[P(\bar X<9)\approx0.0228.\]

questions.prompt: A sample of size \(49\) is drawn from a population with variance \(196\). Find \(\operatorname{sd}(\bar X)\).
questions.answer: The population standard deviation is \(\sqrt{196}=14\). Therefore \[\operatorname{sd}(\bar X)=\frac{14}{\sqrt{49}}=2.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(80\) and standard deviation \(14\). For \(n=49\), estimate \(P(\bar X>83)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(14/7=2\). The z-score is \((83-80)/2=1.5\), so \[P(\bar X>83)\approx1-\Phi(1.5)=0.0668.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(100\) and variance \(400\). For \(n=25\), find the approximate distribution of \(\bar X\).
questions.answer: The standard deviation is \(20\), so the standard error is \(20/5=4\). Thus \(\bar X\) is approximately \(N(100,4^2)\), assuming the sample mean is approximately normal.

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(5\) and standard deviation \(2\). For \(n=81\), estimate \(P(\bar X>5.4)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(2/9=0.2222\). The z-score is \((5.4-5)/0.2222=1.8\), so \[P(\bar X>5.4)\approx1-\Phi(1.8)=0.0359.\]

questions.prompt: For a sample mean, explain why increasing \(n\) from \(25\) to \(100\) changes the standard error by a factor of \(1/2\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(\sigma/\sqrt n\). Changing \(n\) from \(25\) to \(100\) changes \(\sqrt n\) from \(5\) to \(10\), so the standard error is halved.

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(30\) and standard deviation \(6\). For \(n=144\), estimate \(P(29<\bar X<31)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(6/12=0.5\). The z-scores are \(-2\) and \(2\), so \[P(29<\bar X<31)\approx0.9772-0.0228=0.9544.\]

questions.prompt: A sample mean has standard error \(1.5\) from a population with standard deviation \(12\). Find the sample size.
questions.answer: Use \(\sigma/\sqrt n=1.5\). Then \(12/\sqrt n=1.5\), so \(\sqrt n=8\) and \(n=64\).

questions.prompt: A population has \(E(X)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(X)=25\). For \(n=100\), find \(E(\bar X)\) and \(\operatorname{sd}(\bar X)\).
questions.answer: The sample mean has \(E(\bar X)=0\). Its variance is \(25/100=0.25\), so \(\operatorname{sd}(\bar X)=\sqrt{0.25}=0.5\).

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(200\) and standard deviation \(24\). For \(n=36\), estimate \(P(\bar X<196)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(24/6=4\). The z-score is \((196-200)/4=-1\), so \[P(\bar X<196)\approx\Phi(-1)=0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(75\) and standard deviation \(10\). For \(n=100\), find an interval centred on \(75\) that is approximately \(95\%\) likely to contain \(\bar X\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(10/10=1\). A central \(95\%\) normal interval is about \(\pm1.96\) standard errors, so the interval is \[75\pm1.96(1)=[73.04,76.96].\]

questions.prompt: A population has standard deviation \(30\). What sample size gives \(\operatorname{sd}(\bar X)=3\)?
questions.answer: Solve \(30/\sqrt n=3\). Then \(\sqrt n=10\), so \(n=100\).

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(18\) and standard deviation \(12\). For \(n=64\), estimate \(P(16<\bar X<20)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(12/8=1.5\). The z-scores are \(-1.33\) and \(1.33\), so \[P(16<\bar X<20)\approx0.9082-0.0918=0.8164.\]

questions.prompt: A sample of size \(16\) has standard error \(2\). What is the population standard deviation?
questions.answer: Since \(\operatorname{se}=\sigma/\sqrt n\), we have \(2=\sigma/4\). Therefore \(\sigma=8\).

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(120\) and standard deviation \(60\). For \(n=900\), estimate \(P(\bar X>122)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(60/30=2\). The z-score is \((122-120)/2=1\), so \[P(\bar X>122)\approx1-\Phi(1)=0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A sample mean has approximate distribution \(N(40,0.25^2)\) and the population standard deviation is \(5\). Find the sample size.
questions.answer: The standard error is \(0.25\), so \(5/\sqrt n=0.25\). Hence \(\sqrt n=20\) and \(n=400\).

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(10\) and standard deviation \(5\). Find \(P(9<\bar X<11)\) for \(n=100\), using a normal approximation.
questions.answer: The standard error is \(5/10=0.5\). The z-scores are \(-2\) and \(2\), so \[P(9<\bar X<11)\approx0.9772-0.0228=0.9544.\]
